gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Cable Matters active 48Gbps extension only works with its female socket facing the source and its male plug in the display, so it can extend a run only at the TV end. Reversed, for example as a short port-saver plugged into a PS5 or PC, it 'will not work'.
standout_why: Compared against the cited iTechGuides guide, the cited Cable Matters page and ChatGPT's answer. iTechGuides says only that active cables are 'normally directional', with ends marked Source/Display, and that reversing them 'generally will not work'. It never says which end of a male-to-female extension is the source end. ChatGPT just wrote 'directional'. The Cable Matters page does say 'female connector must be connected to the source device', but ChatGPT left out that practical consequence. The UGREEN HD151 cited page (bestways.com) returned HTTP 429, so I could not read it. hdmi.org's Ultra High Speed cable page says nothing about extension cables.
decides: The active Cable Matters cable fits only setups where the extension is the last piece before the TV (source → existing cable → female socket → active extension → male plug into TV). It can't be the short stub plugged into a console or GPU, which is a common reason people buy one. For that use, or when the direction is unknown, the passive UGREEN HD151 is the safer pick, with no direction or USB power to manage. The Cable Matters cable may also need its Micro-B USB power lead, which Cable Matters calls 'optional but recommended' for longer runs or 8K. That's because a source supplies extra cable power only if it supports HDMI Cable Power, according to hdmi.org.

findings.label: HDMI Cable Power: why active cables carry a USB lead
findings.value: Active cables can draw power from the HDMI connector only if both the cable and the source support HDMI Cable Power. Otherwise they need a separate power connector (typically USB Micro-B or USB-C). Reversed active cables cause no damage but do not work.
findings.note: hdmi.org wording: cables 'include a separate power connector for use with source devices that do not support the HDMI Cable Power feature'. 'active cables can only be attached in one direction'. The page gives no current figure.

findings.label: Scope of Ultra High Speed certification
findings.value: The certification program covers cables named 'Ultra96 HDMI Cable and Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable'. They need a certification label on the package and the name on the jacket. The page does not mention extension, male-to-female or coupler cables.
findings.source_title: Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable - Bandwidth Up To 48Gbps
findings.note: Neither candidate's page I opened (Cable Matters) claims the certification label.
